Press Release:


Dark days for Eskom
It’s not just an immediate liquidity crisis. Eskom is on a knife edge and its future fiscal status looks equally dire. Minister Lynne Brown this week openly admitted that load shedding could become a way of life for South Africans. But, is Eskom doing all it can to cut operational costs? Carte Blanche investigates unpaid bills to key maintenance contractors and evidence of serious wasteful expenditure.


Script:


Visuals Script

VO: 8”
Here we are yet again facing more power cuts. If only we’d opened the grid to Independent power producers when the ISMO bill was tabled in parliament 4 years ago we wouldn’t have Eskom’s new CEO Tshediso Matona saying this….

Tshediso Matona:
Every time we have to loadshed it really pains us but we have to loadshed as an act of responsibility because we have a responsibility to prevent a total breakdown blackout of the system as it were.

VO: 3”
Eskom is running out of steam says economist Iraj Abedian.

Iraj:
On all divisions Eskom is malfunctioning – we are not managing operations well, we are not managing supply chain well, we are not managing planning well – we are not managing maintenance well.

VO: 15
It came as no surprise to millions of South African’s many of whom had spent the weekend lighting candles, powering up generators and venting on social media. Mike who didn’t want to be identified was bored in the dark so he started up a facebook page.

Mike:
People are wasting money buying takeaways, they can’t cook, they can’t work so people out there can’t work.
VO: 11”
It’s gone viral – in a week his membership has grown to well over 20000. There’s lots of hot air – but in true South African style members have kept their sense of humour.

.

VO: 8”
We’ll have to keep that sense of humour for a while longer says energy expert Chris Yelland.

Chris:
The energy availability factor has declined from target of 80% down to 76% and this is a very significant about turn largely resulting from deferred maintenance over extended periods of time.


Whoosh Maintenance
April 2014 VO: 12”
The result: we’ve seen evidence of 3 major breakdowns at 3 of our aging fleet this year. First there was Duvha power station – unit three broke down and according to Eskom spokesman Andrew Etzinger the problem persists.

Andrew:
Unit 3 was the subject of an over pressurization incident earlier this year and that unit is still out of operation.

VO: 12”
Then in November a silo collapsed at Majuba in Mpumalanga causing extensive damage. Coal is now being trucked in round the clock to feed the plant. And we’ve learnt there’s a second cracked silo at the station.




Move Iraj bites Andrew:
We’ve known about a crack at the top of silo 30 as its called, for some time now – it doesn’t pose a potential risk nevertheless its part of the investigation.

Iraj:
It’s much like driving a car, the mechanic has told you 2 years ago that your tyres need to change, but you keep driving so don’t be surprised when one if not four of the tyres collapses.

VO: 15
This week it emerged Lethabo power station, which contributes about 10% to the national grid was buried beneath tons of ash. Resident Neal Swanepoel says he’s worried about the potential health hazards .

Neil:
It’s a non stop constant flow of large amount of ash and smoke coming out of those stacks and it just hasn’t stopped. Where usually it will come and go if they have had a problem but of late they just don’t seem to be doing anything about it.

VO: 8”
Residents complained that the power stacks were pumping out excessive smoke covering nearby suburbs and houses.

Neil:
If you live in this Vaal you smoke a packet of cigarettes a day if you like it or not!

Andrew:
Lethabo is one of our oldest power stations so it was built at a time when these considerations were not important. It is in terms of the environmental performance not meeting the current requirements.


Shorter VO: 19”
Eskom admits they are having a problem with ash handling at the plant and we learnt that 2 of the 6 generating units are unable to function. Minister of Public Enterprises, Lynne Brown says the utility needs to address systemic failures.



Lynn:
It’s often between keeping the lights on and doing the maintenance…so the decision is that maintenance has to happen.

VO: 4”
The Minister has an international expert auditing our power stations.

Lynn:
To look at what in particular, whether it has to do with boilers or turbines or any of the other technical areas we know what we should be doing in terms of maintenance.

Whoosh Medupi and Kusile

.
VO: 6”
The situation wouldn’t be quite so dire if Medupi and Kusile were on stream.

Chris:
Actually they are running ten years late at the moment they account for something like 25% of the country’s generating capacity and when you are 10 years late on 25% of the generating capacity something has got to give.

VO: 20”
Violent labour unrest and strikes delayed construction by a year. The first unit, unit 6 at Medupi is scheduled for synchronization on Christmas eve, but South Africans will now have to wait till mid January for thei r anticipated Christmas present.

Matona:
If it means, extending this for a week or two weeks do it, rush because you don’t want to take 7 years building a machine and then rush because you want to meet the deadline and set yourself back.

VO: 11”
But it will take months before the unit goes into commercial operation says DA shadow minister for public enterprises – Natasha Michael.

Devi:
When is it actually going to start generating electricity?

Natasha:
About 6 months in to the initial switch on.

Devi:
What – June?

Natasha:
Somewhere around there it will start producing electricity because all the tests have to be done..

Kusile poisoned power fly by Devi:
And Kusile?

Natasha:
When is that going to come online? Again, nobody knows for sure – this is the answers we keep getting.

VO:
Even if Medupi comes on stream in June – reliable energy will still be an obstacle to growth.


Iraj:
If you are aspiring or planning to have growth of 3%, 5%, 7% Medupi and Kusile – all of that is totally irrelevant. Because all of that coming online will allow this economy to grow at 2% - at best.

Whoosh Financial crisis

VO: 8”
Judging by the results released this week Eskom are feeling the pinch – fuel costs are escalating and municipal debt mounting to 4 billion rand.

Chris:
Eskom is relying extremely heavily on debt, its weakening its balance sheet, and ultimately it results in a credit rating downgrade, which push up the cost of high debt and this eventually has to be passed through to the customers, high price increases, demand for electricity drops, low sales, high costs… no profit.

VO: 12”
Eskom contractors say Eskom can’t afford to pay them. Daniel is representing a group of distribution network contractors in KZN who say they are owed more than 80 million rand because Eskom overspent their budget.

Daniel:
We were told that they had no money. That’s the reason, they don’t have funding….

VO:
An Eskom employee admits the budget was overspent in this audio recording.

.Audio
Anyone who has had an over expenditure of 355m rand and is still owing 100m, that’s nearly half a billion that was nowhere to be found.

Daniel:
A lot of contractors closed down that I know of personally, people losing their houses their vehicles, staff …its just shot up the unemployment rate drastically.

VO: 2”
Eskom admits they were at fault.

Audio
Let me say it in front of everybody here – it was because of our incompetence, in Eskom, the staff, including me, that we allowed that to happen.

VO: 3”
Andrew found the allegations hard to swallow.

Andrew:
We certainly have money to honour the contracts that we have, but I’d have to get more information about this, but its highly unlikely that we don’t have the money.

VO: 5”
In a belated attempt to save money Eskom is now declaring a dispute with the contractors over costs.


VO: 8”
And while the contracts are on hold 100’s of thousands of rands worths of Eskom equipment is sitting stranded on sites across the province.

Daniel:
And after such a long time in the field it doesn’t become an asset to Eskom anymore.

Andrew:
If you’re sloppy in housekeeping, if you are not doing adequate stock control, management of equipment and spares, that leads to fatalities as well so its very important for us ….particularly our regions are regularly inspected for wastage.

Whoosh salaries and bonuses?

VO: 6
Given all of this why is the board approving fat salaries and bonuses?

Natasha:
We’ve got people earning the highest salaries in the country and they can’t keep the lights on and that is unacceptable.

Matona:
Based on research they are not. They are not. They are actually in the lower quarter compared to their peers and in fact they have no peers.

VO: 12”
Which may explain why Brian Dames the former CEO earned nearly 23 million rand last year –that’s R62 000 a day.

Matona:
The complexity, span of control, might I say stress of the job of Eskom and given what they are paid, in fact actually we need a correction of that situation.

Iraj:
All the state owned enterprises have taken really a life of their own, which is a life of extraction to the maximum irrespective of its consequences for economic as well as political situation.

VO:
This week there was an urgent debate in parliament to discuss the Eskom crisis. WeBut need to shift focus away from Eskom to a new national energy policy.


Independent Services and Market Operator bill
VO: 4”
First step tabling ISMO bill to open up the energy sector.

Natasha:
Eskom enjoys a monopoly in our country and if the ISMO bill is passed it means independent power producers will have the opportunity to add onto the grid and the ANC for some reason is blocking this bill even though the president has twice said that this bill will be brought before parliament.

VO: 5”
It’s now up to government to make sure there’s light at the end of the tunnel.

Iraj:
At the moment government has not shown its hand so to speak so we don’t know whether they are in denial, whether they are in the process of hammering out a new policy or whether they don’t know what to do.


Promo 1:

VO: 5”
Eskom’s running out of steam but executives are picking up fat pay cheques.

Matona:
Stress….


Promo 2:
VO: 6”
Thousands of rands worth of Eskom equipment abandoned, contractors owed millions and on the brink of bankruptcy…

Daniel:
Lost their houses….

VO: 2”
Isn’t it time Eskom tightens its belt?


Promo 3

VO: 3”
Our aging fleet of power stations limp along…

Iraj:
Car analogy
